title: Models for EDPs Relocation and Relative Policies

context_sources.name: UNHCR Global Trends: Forced Displacement in 2017
Paris Agreement 2015, intended nationally determined contributions
Wang, human capital and regional growth convergence, 2013

limitations: Watermark glyphs leak into the text and break several formulas.
The accessibility formula and the culture-score aggregation are reconstructed from prose.
The threat-class table gives two classes the same interval and skips one.
Result tables are images, so only numbers repeated in prose could be checked.

tasks: Define who counts as environmentally displaced and count them
Allocate people to destinations within capacity
Measure policy effects on economy, crime, language and emissions
Apply the whole chain to one country

section_map.summary: Three parts: planning with two new states and a relocation model, four policy fields, Maldives application.
The legal gap: the refugee convention expanded and still does not cover this group.
Most stay home, sea level only rises, emissions per head fixed, one crisis at a time, crime is rational.
EWS and PEWS, a Red List style culture score, then a five-indicator destination index with a cap.
Labor model, crime time allocation, language attrition, blended emissions.
127,200 to Australia, 107,200 to Sri Lanka, 205,600 to India, and one revised emissions ceiling.
AHP consistency ratio 0.055. Labor model hold-out errors under 5 percent.
Four strengths tied to borrowed instruments. Two weaknesses, both about scope.

contributions.summary: Two declared states that turn a whole population into a legally recognized group.
A culture score copied from the species Red List, including bins for missing data.
Crime reduced to a time allocation whose derivative signs the policy.

dependency_graph.handoff: The culture indicators, reweighted, become the cultural similarity term inside the culture pull index
The band structure of the culture score prices the language loss at 0.825 points per step
The allocation headcounts are the arrivals that shift each destination's emissions

assumptions.summary: Most people stay in their own country because leaving is harder and entry rules are strict.
Per-capita emissions are unchanged by moving.
Everyone is a rational maximizer, and switching between legal and illegal work is free.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Australia 1990-2012 for the labor model; World Bank indicators for pollution; populations and accounts in the appendix.

models.summary: Eight cultural indicators, three weights, eight threat classes.
Five-indicator suitability, AHP weights, 0.5 percent cap, accessibility side objective.
Cobb-Douglas with a hidden technology term and a contribution ratio.
Four-state expected utility over legal and illegal time.
Speaker count compounded by death or birth.
Population-weighted blend of pollution and emissions.

verification.summary: AHP consistency ratio 0.055, below 0.1, largest eigenvalue 5.2203.
Labor model hold-out on 2013-2016: errors 4.3, 2.4, 1.4, 3.1 percent.

results_trace.summary: Australia: human capital elasticity 0.923, contribution to growth 70.4 percent.
Maldives: 127,200 to Australia, 107,200 to Sri Lanka, 205,600 to India.
Australia's carbon dioxide ceiling raised to 359,462 thousand metric tons.

writing_logic.summary: A definition is settled before any counting, and a named country's public statement is the test.
The benefit of arrivals and the risk of backlash are stated together, and the cap follows from the risk.
High crime is blamed on non-acceptance, which redirects the remedy from policing to opportunity cost.

language_observations.summary: The group is given a mission, to carry the culture, before any model appears.
The scoring system includes explicit bins for insufficient data and for cases never assessed.
Crime is denied a moral cause in one clause and redefined as time allocation in the next.
Innovation is defined as moving a method between fields, then shown twice.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1: the three-part restatement, planning, policy, application.
Figure 2: comparison supporting the claim that most people stay.
Figure 3: the three UNHCR categories of displaced people.
Figure 4: how the two new states map onto those categories.
Figure 7: the culture evaluation system and its classes.
Figure 8: the five-indicator climate similarity score.
Figure 9: which culture indicators policy moves.
Figure 10: speaker trajectories with and without protection.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Inventing a status that a country must declare, and that others must recognize, makes the model start from a political act.
Rejecting the moral explanation before modeling forces the remedy to be structural.
Stating the backlash risk in the same breath as the benefit keeps the cap from looking arbitrary.

weaknesses.summary: The threat classes overlap: two labels share 40-60 and the 20-40 band is absent.
Suitability and accessibility are never combined; the Maldives plan uses only the ranking and the cap.
Authors: no model of sea level itself, and nothing for people displaced by failing agriculture.

independent_extensions.summary: Repair the class intervals so every band has one label.
Solve the two objectives jointly instead of ranking on one and capping.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Rescale incomparable indicators before weighting, and say which two methods cross-check the weights.
Give each policy its mechanism and its measured consequence, not just its aim.

unresolved_questions.question: Which score band belongs to which threat class, given the collision at 40-60?
How are suitability and accessibility weighed against each other when they conflict?
